f2_source.finding: _canonical_relpath enforces non-empty canonical POSIX syntax, no NUL/backslash, no absolute path and no dot/dot-dot segment. It does not enforce Windows reserved-name rules or detect distinct manifest paths that collapse under Windows case-insensitive semantics.

external_sources.finding: Windows guidance says not to assume case sensitivity; forbids reserved characters; reserves CON/PRN/AUX/NUL/COM1..9/LPT1..9 families even with extensions; and advises against trailing spaces or periods.
PureWindowsPath comparisons are case-insensitive and PureWindowsPath.is_reserved() is available in the existing Python 3.12 baseline for offline Windows-flavour lexical checks.

findings.statement: A release manifest constructed on a case-sensitive builder can represent two lexically distinct POSIX paths that are not distinct under default Windows path semantics. The current manifest schema checks exact-string duplicate paths only, so it lacks a portable materialization collision invariant.
findings.cheapest_falsifier: Construct a synthetic manifest/package containing two regular entries whose relative paths differ only by Windows case folding (for example, A/file.txt and a/file.txt) on a case-sensitive builder. A future portable-path validator should reject before host handoff.

findings.statement: The current canonical POSIX path grammar can admit components such as NUL.txt or names ending with a dot/space that are problematic or reserved under ordinary Windows path semantics. A portable release contract should either reject such components or explicitly declare Windows materialization out of scope.
findings.cheapest_falsifier: Feed representative reserved/invalid Windows components through _canonical_relpath; current source is predicted to accept several of them because it does not apply a Windows-flavour portability profile.

current_tree_scan.observed: A recursive Git tree was requested and no targeted exact reserved-name hit was found in the surfaced result, but the connector response is too large/truncated to honestly certify absence of all case-fold/reserved-name collisions.
current_tree_scan.next_discriminator: Add or run a deterministic repository/release-manifest portability linter over the exact release candidate; do not infer current-tree cleanliness from a truncated tree view.

shape: Keep canonical POSIX path identity as the manifest's serialization form.
Additionally compute a Windows-flavour collision key for each component/path using stdlib-only PureWindowsPath/case semantics or an explicitly specified equivalent.
Reject reserved Windows path components and trailing dot/space if Windows is an admitted portable target.
Reject any pair of release paths that collapse to the same portability key.
Keep this as deterministic pre-handoff validation; do not let host filesystem behavior become a second manifest authority.

counterhypotheses: The portable distribution contract may intentionally target only case-sensitive filesystems; if so, Windows must be explicitly excluded rather than implicitly assumed portable.

The exact release payload may currently contain no colliding/reserved paths. That would make this preventive hardening rather than a present payload defect, but it would not close the missing invariant for future releases.
next_exact_action: Do not advance this objective beyond E1 until an exact release-candidate path set can be scanned deterministically; prioritize the already-E2 junction/release-tree boundary first because it is the stronger current architectural risk.
